verdict.reasoning: Patient reports left-sided hearing difficulty for about six weeks: "I just feel I can't really hear as well as I used to..." and later clarifies it is "just the left ear" and duration "about six weeks."
Patient describes intermittent ringing in the left ear: "I occasionally get like a ringing in my left ear, uh just on the one side."
Patient mentions intermittent dizziness/off-balance: "there's actually been a few times when I felt kind of a bit sick or a bit dizzy" and later clarifies "just a little bit kind of off balance."
Symptoms are intermittent and triggered by TV/music: "it's kind of on and off" and "for example, if I'm watching TV or listen to music or something that'll solve the ringing in the ear."
Right ear unaffected: Doctor asks if difficulty is both ears or just left; patient responds "Uh just the left ear" and doctor says "Alright, so your right ear is fine."

Denies ear pain, discharge, and fever: Doctor asks about pain and discharge ("have you had any pain from the ear at all?"; "Any discharge coming out of the ear? No, OK.") and fever ("have you been experiencing any fever?"); patient does not report any, and the doctor proceeds as if negative, consistent with denial.

Dizziness is mild, not room-spinning vertigo, and not associated with significant nausea: "nothing major" and "it's not the kind of dizziness you get with nausea, like uh not, not proper room spinning or anything like that but just, just a little bit kind of off balance." The fact’s phrasing of "occasional mild nausea" is slightly different, but the patient specifically distinguishes from nausea, so overall description of mild, non-vertiginous dizziness is supported; nausea element is not emphasized but not in direct contradiction.
Prior similar brief episode ~1 year ago: "I had something maybe, about a year ago, but it only lasted a couple of days, it wasn't anything as long as this."

Denies using cotton buds: Doctor asks, "do you use cotton ball buds to try and clean out wax from your ears?" Patient replies, "Uh nah I'll do it" (interpreted as not doing it), and doctor responds, "No, OK. Well, you're right, you should, you shouldn't be doing that."
Summary matches transcript: left unilateral hearing disturbance and intermittent tinnitus for six weeks, no ear pain/discharge/fever, triggered by TV/music, all explicitly described in prior quotes.

Mild intermittent non-vertiginous dizziness and imbalance: "a few times when I felt kind of a bit sick or a bit dizzy" and later "nothing major" and "not proper room spinning or anything like that but just, just a little bit kind of off balance."

Plan for face-to-face otoscopy in 4–5 days to assess for blockage vs other pathology: "we book you in for a face-to-face appointment in one of our clinics... within the next four, five days or so" and "one of the GPs will just have a quick look in the ear and figure out whether there's physical blockage or whether there's something else going on."

Provide tinnitus leaflet link: "I'm going to, uh, put paste the link for a leaflet about Tinnitus, um, in the notes for this appointment. I'd really appreciate it if you could start reading about it."

GP to evaluate exam findings and guide next steps re blockage vs inner ear/balance issue: "we'll be a step closer to figuring out which way we... It might be that there's a problem inside the drum or the balance system within the ear. But, we just need to exclude whether there's physical blockage first."

Patient to call support team to schedule, and to book another video consult if issues arise: "you can ring the support team... then they'll slot you in" and "If there's any problem, any issues between now and when the clinic appointment is, just book another appointment and you can speak to one of us over video."
